title: Define SLI fidelity tiers and preemptive evacuation criteria for multi-region model endpoints
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: Produce an actionable SLI/SLO taxonomy (fidelity tiers) per endpoint and per model variant that drives automated preemptive evacuation and load-shedding decisions across regions. This ticket covers: 1) a compact SLI set (latency P95/P99, availability, response-quality proxy) and normalized fidelity tiers (gold/silver/bronze) 2) concrete thresholds and hysteresis for multi-region evacuation triggers 3) interaction rules with circuit breakers and token-aware load-shedding 4) runtime feature flags and rollout checklist 5) required dashboards and runbook links. Motivation: We observed several incidents where degraded region-level HW/KV-cache state caused sudden quality regressions and cascading failovers. Current SLOs are high level and do not express differentiated fidelity guarantees by route or model variant, nor do they map to an evacuation decision matrix with hysteresis and cost-aware preemption. Deliverables: - SLI definitions (units, tags, measurement windows) for route/model/variant; include exemplars for chat-standard, chat-low-latency, and embedding endpoints. - Fidelity tiers described in operational terms: SLO targets, error-budget burn rules, and protective slices. - Evacuation trigger matrix: per-region thresholds, sustained vs spike rules, cooldown periods, and cross-region capacity reservations. - Circuit-breaker interplay: when CB trips, what fidelity tier downgrades, and when to gracefully evict traffic vs queue. - Load-shedding ordering: tenant/route priority, token-length-aware heuristics, and safe degradation steps (quantized model fallback, response truncation, approximate embeddings). - Observability: metric names, dashboards, and alerting thresholds. - Runbook snippets for on-call and post-incident follow-ups. Acceptance criteria: - Documented SLI list and fidelity tier table stored in Confluence (link below). - A companion simulator run demonstrating evacuation decisions on synthetic traffic (PR in GH). - Updated rollout checklist and feature flag gating for gradual enablement. - Sign-off from Reliability, Product, and Platform Security.

notes: Key trade-offs: - Aggressive evacuation reduces blast radius but increases cross-region traffic and cost; policy must be cost-aware and respect reserved capacity for enterprise tenants. - Prefer conservative spike thresholds with short hysteresis to avoid flapping. - For Private deployments, evacuation must be optional (customer opt-in) and documented. Open questions: - Should quality SLI use a model-aware proxy (QA eval on sampled requests) or a heuristic (response length + logits)? - How to account for bursty long-token requests in token-normalized burn accounting?
next_steps: 1) Finalize SLI definitions and run full simulation sweep (tokens, KV-hit/miss, cold-cache). 2) Implement GA dashboards and alerts (pair with Observability team). 3) Create feature-flag-controlled rollout on canary subset of routes for 2 weeks. 4) Schedule reliability tabletop to validate runbook and customer communications.
